cmad.notes: SDO is an operating NASA mission (launched 11 February 2010, no StopDate), so a CMAD is expected. One SDO CMAD was located, and only for the EVE instrument: 'SDO EVE Calibration and Measurement Algorithms Document Rev B' (LASP, 2025, https://doi.org/10.25810/nh0m-ze62), whose named front-matter authors are A. R. Jones, T. N. Woods, D. L. Woodraska, R. J. Borelli, P. C. Chamberlin (spelled 'Chamberlain' in the deposited metadata) and F. G. Eparvier. Because Rev B carries a 2025 date, well inside the operating span, its names are treated as current-team evidence. An earlier pre-launch revision also exists: EVE CMAD Rev A, Document No. EVE-T-11003, dated 31 January 2005 (https://soma.larc.nasa.gov/lws/pdf_files/4.2a%20CMAD%20SDO-EVE.pdf), prepared by Francis G. Eparvier as EVE Project Scientist and approved by 'TNW' (Thomas N. Woods); it predates launch by five years, so its names are founding-era rather than current-team evidence. No AIA CMAD and no HMI CMAD were found, and no mission-wide SDO CMAD was found, after searching (a) DataCite, which indexes only three heliophysics CMADs in total and for SDO only the EVE Rev B document, (b) the provider data centres (lmsal.com/sdodocs document index, hmi.stanford.edu, lasp.colorado.edu/eve, sdo.gsfc.nasa.gov) and (c) general web search plus the NASA LWS/SOMA programme library. This is a real gap: the SDO 2020 Senior Review Proposal budgeted AIA, EVE and HMI CMAD production for FY21-FY23 (Sections 3.1-3.4 and Appendix B), so AIA and HMI CMADs were planned but are not publicly locatable. Current-team evidence for AIA and HMI therefore rests on the provider pages and the SPASE Instrument records instead.

instrument_coverage.notes: The Observatory record has no downward instrument links, so the SPASE side was established by reverse lookup: the three records under SMWG/Instrument/SDO/ (AIA, EVE, HMI) were each opened and each carries ObservatoryID spase://SMWG/Observatory/SDO. Ground truth for the payload came from three independent sources that agree exactly: the SDO mission instruments page (which also names a PI and PI institution for each of HMI, AIA and EVE), the mission overview paper (Pesnell et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9841-3), and the Observatory record's own Description ('The spacecraft carries three instruments'). SDO's payload is genuinely three instruments, so SPASE coverage is complete and nothing is missing. Note that EVE is an instrument suite with named subsystems (MEGS with channels A, B, SAM and P; ESP; EEB) and HMI/AIA share the Joint Science Operations Center at Stanford; none of these subsystems has its own SPASE Instrument record, which is consistent with how the mission itself counts three instruments.

pending_instrument_runs.reason: paper-selection uncertain - two co-equal HMI description papers
pending_instrument_runs.notes: HMI has two description papers published side by side in the same Solar Physics SDO special issue, and neither is clearly the single authoritative one: the investigation paper (Scherrer et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9834-2, 13 authors, ~2300 citations) and the design and ground-calibration paper (Schou et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9842-2, 21 authors, ~1800 citations). The HMI SPASE Instrument record links neither. For this Observatory run the ambiguity turns out not to matter, because both papers name the same three leads in their first three positions - Scherrer, Schou and Bush - so all three are recorded at full strength with both papers cited. A dedicated HMI run must still settle which paper is the instrument's reference before taking its 4th and 5th authors. The HMI run should also harvest the HMI science-team page (http://hmi.stanford.edu/ScienceTeam/index.html), which lists roughly 35 Co-Investigators and Associated Investigators with explicit per-person roles across Stanford, LMSAL, HAO and 15 other institutions; that roster is instrument-team depth and was deliberately not swept into this Observatory-level list.

notes: Operating span: the Observatory record has no OperatingSpan element, so the start date was taken from its Description ('SDO was successfully launched on 11Feb2010'), corroborated by the SDO 2020 Senior Review Proposal mission fact sheet (launched 11 February 2010, prime mission from 1 May 2010). SDO is still operating, so the stop is null. The overview paper (2011 online, 2012 in print) and all three instrument papers fall inside the expected 2-5 year window around the start of operations.

Mission overview paper selection is confident: (Pesnell et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9841-3) is titled exactly 'The Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)', is the lead paper of the Solar Physics SDO special issue, has ~3200 Crossref citations, and Crossref and Semantic Scholar return the same paper with the same three authors. Its author list is not alphabetized (Pesnell, Thompson, Chamberlin), so all three positions carry contribution order and all three are Strong. The same three people are the special issue's guest editors, which independently corroborates them as the mission-level leads.

AIA author-order detection: the 47-name list of (Lemen et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9776-8) is not one sorted run but a sequence of institution blocks each sorted internally - LMSAL from Akin to Yanari, then the Smithsonian group from Bookbinder, then Stanford, then LLNL, e2v and Rutherford Appleton. A strict backward scan finds only a four-name sorted suffix (Beardsley, Clapp, Lang, Waltham) because the block boundaries break the sort, but the substantive pattern is unmistakable: alphabetization begins at author 3. Taking the conservative reading, the deliberately ordered prefix is Lemen and Title only, and they are the sole AIA paper authors given position-based evidence. Akin, Boerner and everyone after them owe their places to the alphabet, not to contribution.

EVE author-order detection: backward scan of the 18-name list of (Woods et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-009-9487-6) finds a sorted suffix of five (Bailey, Fuller-Rowell, Sojka, Tobiska, Viereck), making the list partially alphabetized with a 13-name prefix. The affiliation footnotes confirm the structure - the prefix is the institutional working groups (LASP, USC, NRL, Space Systems Research, GSFC, MIT Lincoln Laboratory) in order, and the alphabetized tail is the single-institution co-investigators. On this Observatory run only prefix positions 1-3 (Woods, Eparvier, Hock) are taken; prefix positions 4 onward are instrument-team depth for the EVE Instrument-record run.

HMI author-order detection: neither HMI paper is alphabetized. (Scherrer et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9834-2) has a sorted suffix of only three (Schrijver, Tarbell, Tomczyk) and (Schou et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9842-2) a sorted suffix of only three (Elmore, Norton, Tomczyk); a run that short happens by chance, so position carries contribution order in both. Positions 1-3 of each paper name the same three people in different order - Scherrer, Schou, Bush - so the two-paper ambiguity does not change which HMI leads this run records.

Andrew R. Jones and Donald L. Woodraska sit at EVE paper positions 4 and 5, which carry no weight on an Observatory run. Both are nevertheless included, and entirely through an independent source: they are named authors of the current SDO/EVE CMAD Rev B (Jones et al. 2025, 10.25810/nh0m-ze62). Rita J. Borelli comes in the same way and appears in no paper author list at all.

The CMAD deposit spells the fifth author 'Chamberlain, Phillip C'. This is recorded as Phillip C. Chamberlin - the same person as the mission overview paper's third author and the EVE prime-mission science team member at LASP - but a curator should confirm the spelling against the document itself, which could not be downloaded because the CU Scholar repository refuses automated requests; the author list came from the DataCite record for the DOI.

Provider pages disagree with SPASE on the current AIA PI, and SPASE is the more recent. The SDO mission instruments page still names Alan Title as AIA PI, and aia.lmsal.com still directs enquiries to Mark Cheung, while the AIA SPASE Instrument record carries Meng Jin as PI with Cheung, Schrijver and Title as FormerPI. Meng Jin's own staff page at LMSAL dates his AIA PI role from 2022, which resolves the conflict in SPASE's favour. All four are recorded, with Title and Cheung as former PIs of AIA and Jin as the sitting one.

The HMI science team page lists roughly 35 Co-Investigators and Associated Investigators with explicit per-person roles. On an Observatory run that whole roster is instrument-team depth, so it was deliberately not swept in; only people already qualifying by another route (Scherrer, Schou, Bush, Title, Schrijver) had their HMI roles attached, and the roster is flagged in pending_instrument_runs for the HMI Instrument-record run. The same applies to the EVE personnel page's prime-mission science team and LASP engineering staff, and to the AIA paper's 45 co-authors.

The Observatory record's RevisionHistory attributes the 2026-07-20 update to the initials 'JWL' with no full name. Initials alone are not a person, and a metadata updater would be excluded anyway, so no candidate was created; noted here for the audit trail.

Rock I. Bush has no Person record. A record exists at spase://SMWG/Person/R.Bush but its affiliation is the University of California, Berkeley, whereas the HMI Rock I. Bush is at Stanford University, so the two were treated as different people and person_record was left null. A curator should confirm before reusing the existing record.

Person records are missing for seven included candidates: Phillip C. Chamberlin, Wei Liu, Francis G. Eparvier, Rachel A. Hock, Andrew R. Jones, Rita J. Borelli, Jesper Schou and Rock I. Bush. Madhulika Guhathakurta has a record in the published registry (https://spase-metadata.org/SMWG/Person/Madhulika.Guhathakurta.html) that is absent from the local SMWG clone, so the clone is not a complete mirror and existence checks were confirmed against the live registry.

Barbara J. Thompson is widely described as SDO Deputy Project Scientist, but no primary source naming her in that role was located during this run, so she is recorded on her mission overview paper authorship alone and carries no contact role. SPASE has no role for a deputy project scientist in any case.

Rachel A. Hock appears in the SDO papers only as 'R. Hock' / 'R.A. Hock' and is not on the current EVE personnel page. The given name is taken from her lead authorship of the EVE MEGS radiometric calibration paper with the same LASP group; downstream identity confirmation is advisable, particularly as she is reported to have later published under a different surname.
